judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya v MOHD IZZUDDIN BIN MD RANI
judgments.catchwords: Tertuduh telah didakwa dengan satu pertuduhan dibawah perenggan 39B(1)(a) Akta Dadah Berbahaya 1952 yang boleh dihukum dibawah subseksyen 39B (2) Akta yang sama. Penilaian kes pendakwaan adalah berdasarkan: Elemen Pertama : Identiti, Jenis dan Berat Dadah Elemen Kedua : Milikan, Jagaan, Kawalan dan Pengetahuan Elemen Ketiga : Anggapan Pengedaran 37(da)(xvi) ADB1952 Setelah meneliti keterangan Pendakwaan secara penilaian maksimum, Mahkamah ini telah memutuskan bahawa wujud satu ke prima facie terhadap Tertuduh dan memerintahkan Tertuduh membela diri. Penilaian kes pembelaan mendapati pembelaan tertuduh hanyalah bersifat penafian dan rekaan semata-mata dan tidak boleh dipercayai atas faktor-faktor seperti berikut: a. Kegagalan memanggil saksi material; b. Ketiadaan aduan rasmi; c. Kegagalan memberikan maklumat awal kepada Pegawai Penyiasat; d. Tiada sokongan dokumentar; dan e. Ketidakkukuhan versi Tertuduh. Berkenaan kegagalan menyiasat CCTV, cap jari dan DNA, mahkamah berpandukan prinsip bahawa di bawah seksyen 134 Akta Keterangan 1950, tiada keperluan bagi bilangan saksi tertentu bagi membuktikan fakta, keterangan seorang saksi yang boleh dipercayai adalah mencukupi, dan keterangan langsung SP3 adalah bukti utama. Mahkamah mensabitkan Tertuduh atas kesalahan sepertimana pertuduhan dan menjatuhkan hukuman penjara 30 tahun dan 12 sebatan.
judgments.judge: YA Dato' Mohd Aimi Zaini bin Mohd Azhar

judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case

Fraud allegations – Order 14 Rule 1(2)(b) exclusion applies only where claim is solely founded on fraud – Alternative causes of action pleaded. Unjust enrichment – Defendant enriched at Plaintiff’s expense – Retention unjust – Restitution ordered. Confirmation of debt – Written agreement acknowledging liability – Partial repayment made – Binding contractual admission. Criminal guilty plea – Section 43 Evidence Act 1950 excludes conviction as conclusive proof – Guilty plea admissible as judicial admission. Forgery – Defendant convicted under Penal Code s.468 for counterfeit prepaid cards – Criminal act formed factual basis of civil liability. Bona fide triable issue – Defendant’s assertions (return of cards, middleman role, harassment) rejected as afterthoughts – No genuine issue disclosed. Counterclaim – Harassment claim unsubstantiated – Unliquidated tort claim cannot set off liquidated debt. Estoppel – Execution of debt acknowledgment estopped Defendant from denying liability. Liquidated debt – Debt quantified and admitted – Recoverable via summary judgment. Abuse of process – Summary procedure exists to prevent delay of admitted debts by baseless defenses – Trial would waste judicial resources.

judgments.title: MUHAMMAD HANIFF RAZRI BIN HASRI v Pendakwa Raya & ors
judgments.catchwords: Criminal Justice - Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, ss. 2, 37(d), 39B(1)(a) — Trafficking — Appeal against conviction — Whether statutory presumption of deemed possession under s. 37(d) can be conflated with substantive trafficking under s. 2 by "keeping and storing" without proof of an independent positive overt act beyond reasonable doubt — Presumption stacking and impermissible inversion of burden of proof — Criminal Procedure Code, s. 180(3) — Duty of trial court to amend charge to possession under s. 39A(2) where only s. 37(d) possession proved at close of prosecution case — Mid-trial mutation of case causing incurable prejudice and breach of natural justice — Evidence Act 1950, s. 54(1) — Prejudicial reception of bad character evidence (AADK document and smoking bong) — Break in chain of custody via non-contemporaneous, post-facto reconstruction of Drug Exhibit Register (POL 260) compromising identity of dangerous drugs — Non-exclusive access to ancestral premises and negative forensic nexus — Curative provisions inapplicable where foundational evidence of possession is fatally tainted — Conviction quashed and substituted conviction under s. 39A(2) refused — Accused acquitted and discharged.

judgments.title: SIVACHANDRAN A/L S JAYARAJAH v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Constitutional Law - Federal Constitution - Articles 5(1), 8(1) and 8(2) Fundamental liberties - Life and personal liberty - Human dignity - Equal protection of the law - Whether it is in violation of medical ethics for medical officer to be participate in the execution of whipping. Judicial whipping - Corporal punishment - Whether judicial whipping amounts to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment (“CIDT”) - Whether punishment of whipping is inconsistent with constitutional protection of life, dignity and bodily integrity. Whether whipping is disproportionate and therefore contrary to Article 8(1) - Whether exemption of women from whipping constitutes prohibited discrimination on ground only of gender is contrary to Art 8(2) - Intelligible differentia. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.
